To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the prevalence of vitamin C deficiency in CKD patients was 50% in diabetic patients and 40% in non-diabetic patients, (2) the prevalence of low plasma vitamin C level was 50% and 30%, respectively, (3) vitamin C deficiency was significantly associated with low serum albumin and high serum creatinine levels in diabetic patients, and (4) low plasma vitamin C levels were significantly associated with low albumin levels in diabetic patients.
